---
title: "Finding unobserved groups"
---

Suppose each vowel token is represented by its first and second formant-frequency measurements. The measurements are observed, but we may fit a model without supplying the elicitation word or intended vowel category as a response label. The linguistic question is whether recurring regions appear in this particular acoustic representation, and, if they do, how those regions relate to categories supplied by the experimental design.

This separation is the **component--category distinction**. A group is unobserved only in the sense that no group label is supplied to the fitting procedure. A fitted cluster or mixture component is not automatically a phoneme, a vowel category, or a dialect group. That interpretation requires a separate comparison with linguistic annotations, held-out measurements, or other external evidence.

## K-means clustering

The analysis begins by [representing each object](representing-objects.qmd) as a row of measurements. This step fixes whether we are grouping vowel tokens, speakers, or some other unit. [Distance and scaling](distance-and-scaling.qmd) then determine which pairs of rows count as similar. Measurements with different units or ranges, for instance, can contribute very differently to Euclidean distance unless the transformation is specified.

[K-means](k-means.qmd) assigns each row to one cluster and represents each cluster by a centroid. The assignment and centroid updates minimize [within-cluster loss](within-cluster-loss.qmd). [Silhouette widths](silhouette-scores.qmd) compare the distance from each row to its assigned cluster with its distance to the nearest alternative. [Validation without labels](unsupervised-validation.qmd) evaluates centroids on rows that were not used to fit them.

## Finite mixture models

A [**finite mixture model**](https://mc-stan.org/docs/stan-users-guide/finite-mixtures.html) represents a distribution as a weighted combination of component distributions. A [Gaussian mixture model](gaussian-mixtures.qmd) uses Gaussian components for the observed measurements. [Posterior membership probabilities](posterior-membership.qmd) quantify how much each component contributes to the density at an observed row. [Expectation-maximization](expectation-maximization.qmd) alternates between updating those membership weights and updating the component parameters.

[Choosing a mixture with BIC](choosing-a-mixture.qmd) compares fitted likelihoods after accounting for the number of parameters. [Held-out mixture validation](validating-a-mixture.qmd) instead evaluates the fitted density for speakers absent during fitting.

The mixture pages use Peterson and Barney's [original vowel study](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.1906875) and a documented version of its [acoustic table](https://www.fon.hum.uva.nl/praat/manual/Create_formant_table__Peterson___Barney_1952_.html). The table contains two productions of each of ten /hVd/ elicitation words by each of 76 speakers. It records F0 and the first three formant-frequency measurements, along with speaker and intended-vowel metadata. We use an F1--F2 subset as an acoustic representation and retain the metadata for interpretation. Thus, neither the measurements nor the fitted components are being treated as phonological categories by definition.

The pages occur in the order needed to keep that distinction visible. First we fix the represented object, geometry, and hard-clustering objective. We then ask what fitted compactness and held-out loss can establish. Finally, we introduce Gaussian components, posterior responsibilities, estimation, model comparison, and validation on speakers absent during fitting. The probability calculations rely on the earlier chapters on [random variables and distributions](../random-variables-and-distributions/index.qmd), while the validation arguments reuse the earlier separation between [training and test data](../model-criticism-and-prediction/training-and-test-data.qmd).
